fixtures: Each file is an agents/*.md definition, copied into the run's data/ folder.

evals.name: claude-agent-to-copilot
evals.prompt: We wrote data/release-captain.md for Claude Code. We're now publishing the plugin for Copilot CLI and Cursor too. What will break?
evals.expected_output: skills: is Claude-only and silently ignored elsewhere, so on Copilot and Cursor the agent runs without changelog-writer and semver-check; name them in the prompt body as an explicit instruction and keep the frontmatter key. tools lists only Claude names, which strips Bash and WebFetch on Copilot; list Copilot's raw names too (bash, view, web_fetch) or drop tools. GitHub's aliases (web, execute, read) do not work in tools. model: sonnet does not resolve on Copilot, which warns and falls back to auto. maxTurns is Claude-only. The file does not need renaming to .agent.md.
assertions: Says the skills: key is ignored on Copilot CLI and Cursor, so the agent runs without changelog-writer and semver-check
Recommends naming the skills in the agent's prompt body as an explicit instruction
Recommends keeping the skills: frontmatter key for Claude Code rather than removing it
Says the Claude-only tools list strips capability on Copilot and recommends adding Copilot's raw tool names (such as bash, view, web_fetch) or omitting tools
Does not recommend GitHub's tool aliases (web, execute, read) as the fix in tools:
Says model: sonnet does not resolve on Copilot CLI, which warns and falls back to auto
Does not say the file must be renamed to .agent.md for Copilot

evals.name: codex-no-agents
evals.prompt: Can I ship data/triager.md as an agent in our Codex plugin? What frontmatter does Codex want?
evals.expected_output: Not in the plugin: Codex plugins carry skills, MCP servers, apps and hooks, never agents, so data/triager.md in the plugin would be ignored. Two ways to get it to Codex users: ship the triage flow as a skill (or in AGENTS.md), which the plugin can carry, or have users add a standalone Codex agent, which is a TOML file in .codex/agents/ (or ~/.codex/agents/) with name, description and developer_instructions, not Markdown frontmatter. The file is fine as-is for Claude Code.
assertions: States that Codex plugins cannot ship agents, so the file would not load from the plugin
Offers carrying the triage flow in a skill (or AGENTS.md) that the plugin can ship
If it describes Codex's own custom agents, places them outside the plugin in .codex/agents/ (or ~/.codex/agents/) as TOML with name, description and developer_instructions, not Markdown frontmatter
Does not report problems with the agent's frontmatter for Claude Code

evals.name: copilot-empty-tools
evals.prompt: In Copilot CLI, `copilot --agent docs-bot -p "update the docs"` fails, and when I did get it running it couldn't read or edit anything. It's agents/docs-bot.md in our docs-kit plugin, copy in data/docs-bot.md. I put tools: [] so it gets everything.
evals.expected_output: Three problems. description is missing, and Copilot requires it (Claude requires it too). tools: [] disables all tools in Copilot; it does not mean all allowed, so omit tools to get everything. Plugin agents are addressed as plugin-name:agent-name, so the bare name docs-bot is rejected; use docs-kit:docs-bot.
assertions: Flags the missing description as required by Copilot CLI
Explains that tools: [] disables every tool in Copilot rather than allowing all
Recommends omitting tools (or listing the tools) to give the agent its tools
Says Copilot plugin agents must be addressed as plugin-name:agent-name, e.g. docs-kit:docs-bot
